text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- After failure of government's tax reform Finance Minister Theo Waigel announces second attempt at parliamentary mediation to reach agreement with opposition Social Democrats and Greens.
- There is still a danger that the low-lying Oderbruch area will be flooded. The German army stabilises the dikes with help of helicopters.
- Prosecutors calls for 11 years in jail for Egon Krenz, East Germany's last hardline communist leader
- German cartel law will be adapted to European regulations. Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt proposes a draft plan.
HANDELSBLATT
- Daimler doubles its profits but the stock exchange is not satisfied. Europe's biggest company shows sales have improved considerably in first half year results. But the shares retreated
- Tough battle to save the Oder dikes in eastern Germany.
- Corruption has increased in Germany according to Transparency International
- Vereinsbank calls on Hypo Bank shareholders to swap shares
- Lufthansa shares. Privatising more of German carrier could be country's second biggest flotation
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Dramatic battle for the dike at Oderbruch
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel says second parliamentary mediation session on tax reform could take place in September
- Bundesbank issues new banknotes
- Vereinsbank launches exchange action for Hypobank shares on Monday
DIE WELT
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl's keeps to plans for big tax reform. Second parliamentary mediation committee meeting planned for September
- Desperate battle to save Oderbruch more tears appear in dike near Hohenwutzen. Thousands of helpers work around the clock
- Prosecutors demand 11 years jail for Egon Krenz, the last hardline communist leader of East Germany
- Serious blow to Germany as an industry location. The failure of the governmnent tax reform unleashes outrage among business leaders
- Cities and local councils fear billions of marks in losses with planned abolition of trading capital tax -- Bonn Newsroom +49 228 260 97160
